thread.title: Close Update: Bullish Economic Data Lifts S&P Out of Slump

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Bullish Economic Data Lifts S&P Out of Slump
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street brushed aside Wednesday's Fed-fueled sell-off and traded higher Thursday as upbeat US economic data and strength in the technology sector snapped a four-day losing streak for the Standard and Poor's 500.
Most of the data that flooded Wall Street Thursday was bullish with a few exceptions, notably data on trade and the housing market.
Led by a surge in aircraft orders, durable goods orders bounced back significantly in August with a 4.5% gain. Excluding the transportation sector, however, orders were up by an anemic 0.1%, well below the estimated +0.5%.
Second quarter GDP remained unrevised at 4.2%, slightly below 4.3% expectations, while Q2 corporate profits rose 2.1% to a record-high $2.01 trillion.
Jobless claims jumped up in the latest survey week, but at 214,000 remains at a 40+ year low, while preliminary business inventories jumped a greater-than-expected 0.8% in August.
Bucking the trend was a wider goods trade deficit, just shy of a record high at $75.8 billion and 5% wider than July's revised $72.5 billion deficit.
And more bad news from the housing markets as pending home sales hit their slowest sales pace since January, down 1.8%, and underscoring the decelerating housing market with four consecutive monthly declines. Year-over-year, pending home sales are down 2.5% as higher interest rates, rising home prices and a dearth of affordable homes continues to plague the sector.
In corporate news, component stock Apple ( AAPL ) led the technology sector higher thanks to an overweight rating from JP Morgan. The remaining FANG stocks followed Apple's lead, giving the Nasdaq a healthy 0.65% gain.
Tesla ( TSLA ) shares were torpedoed after the close after news broke that the US Securities and Exchange Commission was filling charges against the company and its CEO, Elon Musk, for fraud stemming from Musk's now infamous "going-private" tweet. Shares spilled more than 10% lower in after-hours trade.
For Friday, the economic calendar includes August personal income and spending (est +0.4%, +0.3%), the Sept Chicago PMI (est 62.3) and final Sept Univ of MI consumer sentiment index (unchanged at 100.8).
